title: The man who sold the Eiffel Tower

hooks.text: This man sold the Eiffel Tower... for scrap metal.
In 1925, the Eiffel Tower had a buyer. It wasn't for sale.
How do you sell a landmark you don't own?
The easiest scam in history needed one newspaper.
This man sold the Eiffel Tower, and the buyer kept quiet.
Paris almost lost the Eiffel Tower to a con man.

hookVariants.visual: Tower behind the con man, SOLD slams on 'sold'; tilt up the tower, FOR SCRAP METAL on 'scrap metal'.
Open on a FOR SALE sign hanging from the tower's leg, stamped SOLD on 'sold'; pull back to reveal the whole tower and the con man; SOLD + FOR SCRAP METAL on 'scrap metal'.
Open on a fat stack of cash in the con man's hands, SOLD slams on 'sold', rack focus to the tower behind him; FOR SCRAP METAL.

beats.text: This man sold the *Eiffel Tower*... for scrap metal.
beats.visual: Paris day, low angle: the smug con man (top hat, mustache) touches his hat brim, the whole Eiffel Tower sharp behind him; a red SOLD stamp slams onto the tower on 'sold'. On 'Eiffel Tower' the camera booms up and back: the tower fills the frame, he points up at it, grinning, in the bottom-left third; on 'scrap' FOR SCRAP METAL slams under SOLD.

beats.text: Paris, 1925. Victor Lustig is reading the paper when he spots a tiny story.
beats.visual: Cafe terrace (CAFE DE LA PAIX): Lustig behind a newspaper, coffee cup on the table; the camera glides in; on 'spots' his eyes pop up over the paper and LE MATIN / TOWER NEEDS COSTLY REPAIRS fills the frame.

beats.text: The tower is rusting, and repainting it costs a *fortune.*
beats.visual: Insert on the front-page drawing (no words cut by the frame): rust-orange streaks drip down the drawn tower on 'rusting'; on 'repainting' he lowers the paper into his lap, thinking; on 'fortune' his eyes turn into $ signs and he rubs his hands, then a smug grin.

beats.text: So he forges *government* letterhead and becomes a deputy director at the Ministry of Posts.
beats.visual: Night office, desk lamp: Lustig grins with a rubber stamp in hand. Insert on the big MINISTERE DES POSTES letterhead: his ink hand drops the stamp in and slams it on 'government' (red OFFICIAL imprint, camera kick); pull back to his sly grin; a DEPUTY DIRECTOR badge pops onto his chest on 'becomes'.

beats.text: He books a suite at the Hôtel de Crillon and invites *five* scrap dealers.
beats.visual: Gilded hotel suite (HOTEL DE CRILLON tag): Lustig by an easel with a tower drawing; glide to the long white-clothed table as five dealers pop into the gold chairs one by one from 'invites'.

beats.text: His pitch: the city is secretly tearing the tower down. *Seven thousand tons* of iron.
beats.visual: Lustig points at the tower drawing; on 'secretly' four dealers lean in with sly grins; a red X slashes the drawing on 'tearing', Lustig grins evilly; 7,000 TONS lands on 'Seven'; on 'tons' the dealers' eyes turn into $ signs.

beats.text: One dealer, André Poisson, wants it badly. But something feels off.
beats.visual: Close on Poisson (round glasses, mustache), the suite blurred behind: happy, star eyes on 'badly', then a suspicious squint on 'off' (tilted frame).

beats.text: So Lustig makes a confession. He's a corrupt official, and he needs a *bribe.*
beats.visual: Two-shot: Lustig walks in; tighter, higher angle as he leans to Poisson, hand cupped at his mouth (bubble: Psst... I'm a corrupt official.); back to the wide two-shot, BRIBE? burst on 'bribe', Poisson grins.

beats.text: You see, to Poisson, the bribe was the proof. Only a real official would ask for one.
beats.visual: Push into Poisson's eyes: suspicious, then they light up on 'proof'; low side angle on Poisson with his thought bubble: A bribe? He must be REAL.

beats.text: So Poisson pays $20,000, plus *$50,000* more to win.
beats.visual: Insert on the briefcase between them: Poisson's hand passes it to Lustig's as bills burst out; $20,000 counts up to land on '$20,000', + $50,000 lands on '$50,000'; wide two-shot, both laugh as money rains.

beats.text: Within the hour, Lustig is on a train to *Vienna* with the cash.
beats.visual: Golden-hour station, three-quarter view beside the track: Lustig waves from the yellow carriage's window, $ bag up, PARIS → VIENNA on the carriage; the train pulls out to the left on its rails, smoke streaming back over the roof.

beats.text: He waits for the headlines. Nothing. Poisson is too *embarrassed* to report it.
beats.visual: Dip to a lamp-lit Vienna hotel room: close on NOTHING TO REPORT held up, Lustig's eyes over it; on 'Nothing' he drops the paper on the table and shrugs, confused, WEATHER: RAIN propped beside it; whip to Poisson at his desk, hands on his blushing cheeks.

beats.text: So Lustig comes back to Paris and tries to sell the tower *again.*
beats.visual: Back in Paris: Lustig pitches beside a FOR SALE sign to two new dealers, the tower right behind him; AGAIN?! stamps onto the sign on 'again'.

beats.text: This time, the buyer calls the police, and Lustig escapes to *America.*
beats.visual: The buyer on a 1920s telephone handset; a police car pulls in behind him, light flashing, a cop points; Lustig runs past a TO AMERICA signpost toward the ship.

beats.text: But historians have never found a single police report. The only proof might be a con man's *word.*
beats.visual: Archive: a historian with a magnifier pulls the POLICE 1925 drawer open on 'single': empty; he shrugs. Glide over the cabinets to the V. LUSTIG portrait on the wall, which winks on 'word'.
